questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the storage tanks.
The speed of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks in an air brake system.

questions.question: Why is a flapping cargo cover a problem?

options.text: It is acceptable.
It allows air to keep the cargo cool.
It can tear loose.
It can attract birds.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can tear loose.
questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind. A flapping cover can tear loose and uncover the cargo. It can also block the view of drivers behind you.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum allowed total weight of a vehicle and its cargo.
The minimum allowed weight of a trailer.
The maximum allowed weight of a trailer and its contents.
The maximum allowed weight of just the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum allowed total weight of a vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: GVWR is the maximum combined weight of a vehicle and its cargo allowed by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevents wheel lockup.
Prevents the air compressor from overheating.
Prevents the front brakes from being used on ice.
Prevents the brakes from being used if downshifting would be better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents wheel lockup.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What usually happens to bridges in freezing weather?

options.text: They freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
They freeze after other road surfaces freeze.
They freeze before other road surfaces.
They have heaters that prevent them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges usually freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: What should be true about the leaves on a leaf spring?

options.text: They may be broken.
They are not required.
They should not be broken.
They should shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not be broken.
questions.explanation: When checking the suspension, look for broken or missing leaves in leaf springs. Broken leaves are dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must not be driven.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a trailer, what should the trailer height be?

options.text: Higher than the center height of the fifth wheel.
Lower than the center height of the fifth wheel.
The same height as the fifth wheel.
About shoulder height.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lower than the center height of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: The trailer should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel. This way, the trailer will be raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under it.

questions.question: What should you check on a power steering system during inspection?

options.text: The fluid is at the proper level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses do not contain any fluid.
Only small leaks are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the proper level.
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pump, and fluid level in a power steering system. Look for and repair any leaks before driving.

questions.question: How should you turn the steering wheel when backing a trailer?

options.text: Turn the top of the wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.
It does not matter.
It depends on where you are backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing a trailer, turn the top of the steering wheel opposite to where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning, switch the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What is helpful about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They can replace flat mirrors.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors allow drivers to see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects in convex mirrors appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: What should you do to make night driving easier?

options.text: Keep your interior light on.
Set your instrument panel lights as low as possible while still reading the gauges.
Do not take a nap before driving.
Use only low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set your instrument panel lights as low as possible while still reading the gauges.
questions.explanation: A bright interior makes it hard to see outside at night. Turn off the interior light and set your instrument lights to the lowest level that lets you read the gauges.

questions.question: When using a helper to back up your vehicle, where should they stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger side
In front of the driver side
On the side of the truck
Near the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck
questions.explanation: Your helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them. Before backing, agree on hand signals with your helper. Make sure you both understand the signal for "stop."

questions.question: When entering traffic, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Be ready for slow acceleration, especially if your vehicle is loaded.
Make sure you can cross traffic completely without causing problems.
Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic, remember your vehicle is large and needs more space to accelerate. It takes even longer if your vehicle is loaded. Wait for a large gap in traffic before entering. Never assume other drivers will move for you.

questions.question: Which of the following is required emergency equipment?

options.text: Spare electrical fuses.
A loud horn.
A battery-operated flashlight.
Fireworks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spare electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as reflective triangles.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: You can likely drive faster than a train.
Do not rely only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never rely only on warning signals to know if a train is coming. Never try to beat a train across the tracks. If there are multiple tracks, check all tracks in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.

options.text: Double clutching
Double shifting
Triple clutching
Triple shifting

questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions need double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the right speed. Then push in the clutch, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?

options.text: A service brake system
A parking brake system
An emergency brake system
An axle brake system

questions.correctAnswerText: An axle brake system
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: A suspension system:

options.text: Has a weight capacity rating.
Uses pressurized water to support the load.
Can handle any weight load.
Has a minimum weight rating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has a weight capacity rating.
questions.explanation: Manufacturers give suspension systems a weight capacity rating that shows how much weight they can safely carry.

questions.question: If federal inspectors say your vehicle is unsafe, what can they do?

options.text: Take you to a garage to have it fixed.
Formally request that you fix your vehicle's problems.
Call a mechanic for you.
Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector says a vehicle is unsafe, they can remove it from service until it is fixed.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible.
Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to make them move.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or overweight loads need special permits. These vehicles can usually only drive at certain times.
